```json
{
  "winner": "B",
  "reasons": [
    "B's demand evidence is stronger. Three separate forum threads across Zoho, Apple and Microsoft, spanning years, describe the same concrete pain: replies going out from the wrong alias. A's demand evidence is one conditional app review and one Reddit post about why a builder made their own app. Neither shows a payer.",
    "B's acquisition channels are cheap and targeted for a goal of one paying customer in 90 days: Reddit ads on privacy subreddits at roughly $0.50–$4 CPC, and small privacy newsletters at $50–250 per send. A's main paid channel is iOS CPI of about $3.60 per install against a $3.99–$4.99/month subscription. That needs strong retention, and the brief's own case study (Artifact) did not achieve it.",
    "B's scope is small and well defined: map the incoming recipient to the outgoing From address. Building it as a client-side plugin avoids the credential-proxy GDPR burden. A carries open copyright and licensing exposure from summarizing publisher content, and its core feature is being absorbed for free by Apple News, Google News and general chatbots.",
    "Both ideas face saturated, cheap or free competition, so neither has clear whitespace. A's case against is heavier: a well-funded, award-winning team (Artifact) failed in the same category. B's main risk, commodity bundling by free or cheap incumbents, also applies to A."
  ],
  "weakest_evidence_in_loser": "Idea A's willingness-to-pay signal is a single Syft Play Store review ('Revert the UI back and I'll pay'). It is conditional, about UI rather than the AI feature, and the reviewer says they are leaving for Inoreader. A's claim that Bulletin, KhanList, Content Bite and Syft are 'single-developer-shipped' and 'already monetizing small niches' has no source in the brief, so it counts as missing.",
  "confidence_note": "Low-to-moderate confidence. Both briefs show saturated markets with free or sub-$4 incumbents, and neither presents direct evidence of someone paying for a new entrant. B wins mainly on more specific, repeated pain evidence, cheaper targeted reach and a smaller build. Two weaknesses in B remain: several of its forum quotes look like business users (info@ and admin addresses) rather than the privacy-prosumer payer it targets, and a free Thunderbird extension already covers part of the use case."
}
```
